Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1534
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1534
- **Title**: gh-1532 FLAKE: wrap_ansi_line_perf_test timing assertion (2x input = 3.2x time) red on loaded runner
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1532` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 1
- **Additions**: +118
- **Deletions**: -21
- **Created**: 2026-10-11T06:31:08Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-11T07:02:35Z

## PR Description

Closes #1532
### Root Cause

- `expectLinearGrowth` in `test/cli/wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart` took a **single** doubling-ratio sample: ~3.8ms baseline (100k ASCII cells) vs ~7.2ms doubled, gated at 3.2x while linear measures ~2.0x. On a runner contended by release windows, one scheduler steal/GC pause of a few ms inside either `Stopwatch` window inflates that lone sample past 3.2x — the gh-1532 live failure (fa run 38113730068).
- Sub-5ms single-shot timing assertions are inherently unstable on shared runners; median-of-5 per size was not enough because a sustained steal contaminates ≥3 of 5 runs.

### Fix

- `test/cli/wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart` — `expectLinearGrowth` now takes **3 independent doubling attempts** and gates the superlinear guard on the **min** ratio: contention can only add wall time, so the min approaches the uncontended ratio. A genuine regression (~4x+ quadratic shape) still fails under min, in every attempt.
- Added a **meaningful-growth lower bound** (max ratio across attempts must exceed 1.5x; linear ≈ 2x) so the retry-min cannot become a rubber stamp — a degenerate flat measurement now fails (AC2).
- Threaded an injectable `ElapsedUs` clock through `medianWrapMs`/`expectLinearGrowth` (default: real `Stopwatch`, unchanged behavior) so contention is reproduced **deterministically** via `contendedClock` instead of by CI luck.
- No production changes (`wrapAnsiLine` untouched) — the flake was in the test harness only.

### Test Coverage

- RED first: both new tests failed pre-fix (the hermetic seam did not exist; the flat-clock scenario passed the old assertion while asserting nothing).
- `growth assertion survives a contended-runner preemption spike (gh-1532)` — 30ms fake preemption across 3 timed runs of one measurement (~9x ratio for that attempt) is discarded; PASSED.
- `growth assertion rejects a degenerate flat measurement (gh-1532)` — constant clock (ratio 1.0) must throw `TestFailure`; PASSED.
- Guard not weakened: spiking the doubled measurement in **all 3 attempts** still fails with a 7.09x min ratio.
- Perf file: 8/8 PASSED. `dart analyze` clean, `dart format` applied.
- Full unit suite (CI invocation `dart test --exclude-tags integration`): 10235 passed / 0 failed / 10 skipped; full-discovery JSON reporter confirms both gh-1532 tests execute and pass in-suite.

### Notes

- The absolute 100ms-budget tests were not flaking (median-of-5 over ~10–20ms workloads tolerates outliers) and are unchanged.
- Test names unchanged — "2x input <= 3.2x time" still describes the gate, now applied to the best-of-3-attempts ratio.
- The lower bound (1.5x) sits well below the measured linear ratio (~1.9–2.0x locally across all three shapes) and uses the max across attempts, so jitter cannot push it under the bound without also being visible as a measurement failure elsewhere.
- An earlier broad `dart test` run (including integration-tagged suites) hit 13 failures + a native `malloc_consolidate` abort on this loaded runner under a non-CI tag selection; the CI-equivalent unit invocation above is fully green, and targeted runs of the affected integration files are unrelated to this test-only change.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction evictio…

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1534
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1534
- **Title**: gh-1532 FLAKE: wrap_ansi_line_perf_test timing assertion (2x input = 3.2x time) red on loaded runner
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1532` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 1
- **Additions**: +118
- **Deletions**: -21
- **Created**: 2026-10-11T06:31:08Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-11T07:02:35Z

## PR Description

Closes #1532
### Root Cause

- `expectLinearGrowth` in `test/cli/wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart` took a **single** doubling-ratio sample: ~3.8ms baseline (100k ASCII cells) vs ~7.2ms doubled, gated at 3.2x while linear measures ~2.0x. On a runner contended by release windows, one scheduler steal/GC pause of a few ms inside either `Stopwatch` window inflates that lone sample past 3.2x — the gh-1532 live failure (fa run 38113730068).
- Sub-5ms single-shot timing assertions are inherently unstable on shared runners; median-of-5 per size was not enough because a sustained steal contaminates ≥3 of 5 runs.

### Fix

- `test/cli/wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart` — `expectLinearGrowth` now takes **3 independent doubling attempts** and gates the superlinear guard on the **min** ratio: contention can only add wall time, so the min approaches the uncontended ratio. A genuine regression (~4x+ quadratic shape) still fails under min, in every attempt.
- Added a **meaningful-growth lower bound** (max ratio across attempts must exceed 1.5x; linear ≈ 2x) so the retry-min cannot become a rubber stamp — a degenerate flat measurement now fails (AC2).
- Threaded an injectable `ElapsedUs` clock through `medianWrapMs`/`expectLinearGrowth` (default: real `Stopwatch`, unchanged behavior) so contention is reproduced **deterministically** via `contendedClock` instead of by CI luck.
- No production changes (`wrapAnsiLine` untouched) — the flake was in the test harness only.

### Test Coverage

- RED first: both new tests failed pre-fix (the hermetic seam did not exist; the flat-clock scenario passed the old assertion while asserting nothing).
- `growth assertion survives a contended-runner preemption spike (gh-1532)` — 30ms fake preemption across 3 timed runs of one measurement (~9x ratio for that attempt) is discarded; PASSED.
- `growth assertion rejects a degenerate flat measurement (gh-1532)` — constant clock (ratio 1.0) must throw `TestFailure`; PASSED.
- Guard not weakened: spiking the doubled measurement in **all 3 attempts** still fails with a 7.09x min ratio.
- Perf file: 8/8 PASSED. `dart analyze` clean, `dart format` applied.
- Full unit suite (CI invocation `dart test --exclude-tags integration`): 10235 passed / 0 failed / 10 skipped; full-discovery JSON reporter confirms both gh-1532 tests execute and pass in-suite.

### Notes

- The absolute 100ms-budget tests were not flaking (median-of-5 over ~10–20ms workloads tolerates outliers) and are unchanged.
- Test names unchanged — "2x input <= 3.2x time" still describes the gate, now applied to the best-of-3-attempts ratio.
- The lower bound (1.5x) sits well below the measured linear ratio (~1.9–2.0x locally across all three shapes) and uses the max across attempts, so jitter cannot push it under the bound without also being visible as a measurement failure elsewhere.
- An earlier broad `dart test` run (including integration-tagged suites) hit 13 failures + a native `malloc_consolidate` abort on this loaded runner under a non-CI tag selection; the CI-equivalent unit invocation above is fully green, and targeted runs of the affected integration files are unrelated to this test-only change.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction evictio…

The AGENTS.md is long; I have the conventions. Now let me read the full changed file, and check for CI failures files (there are none input — no ci_failures.md, no pr_discussions.md). So CI status unknown; PR description claims all green.

Let me read the full test file.

Key review questions:

1. **Does the fix actually solve the flake?** The contention model: contention can only ADD wall time — that's the claim used for gating on min. But wait: is that claim correct? Contention adds wall time to both `small` and `doubled` measurements. If contention inflates both equally (additive), the ratio inflates when the small measurement is inflated. Ratio = doubled/small. If the small measurement gets +X ms spike and doubled gets none, ratio decreases. If doubled gets spike, ratio increases. Gating on min across attempts: for the min ratio to be inflated, the doubled measurement must be spiked in EVERY attempt while the small one is not. Possible but much rarer. OK.

2. **The `minRatio` guard uses `lessThan(maxLinearRatio)`** — strictly less than 3.2. Measured linear ratio ~2.0x. Fine.

3. **The new spiked test**: `contendedClock(spiked: {6, 7, 8})`. Measurement call order: per attempt, 5 timed runs of small then 5 of doubled. Attempt 1: calls 1-5 small, 6-10 doubled. So spikes {6,7,8} are the first three timed runs of the doubled measurement in attempt 1. Median of 5 = 3rd value after sorting. Spiked values: times ~[t+30, t+30, t+30, t, t] sorted → [t, t, t+30, t+30, t+30], median = t+30. Hmm! Median of 5 with 3 spiked = spiked value. So the doubled median in attempt 1 is ~baseline+30ms ≈ 7.2+30 = ~37ms vs small ~3.8ms → ratio ~9x. That's what the comment says (~9x ratio for that attempt). Attempts 2,3 are unspiked → ratio ~2x → min ratio ~2x → passes. OK.

Wait — but the call counter: each `medianWrapMs` does 1 warm-up (untimed) + 5 timed. The warm-up doesn't call `measure` — it calls `wrapAnsiLine` directly. Yes: `wrapAnsiLine(line, width); // JIT warm-up, untimed` — not through measure. So timed calls: attempt 1: 1-5 small, 6-10 doubled. Correct.

But wait — `asciiProse` uses the shared `_rng = Random(1496)` — the RNG is a top-level final, shared across calls and tests! `build(baseCells)` is called per attempt: `asciiProse(1000)` three times in the growth test, producing *different strings* per attempt since the RNG continues. That's pre-existing behavior (the old code also called build once per size, so old: 2 calls; new: 6 calls per growth test). Different content per attempt adds variance, but content is similar distribution. Not a new issue but the tripled number of `build` calls consumes the shared RNG stream, which changes what subsequent tests generate — no correctness issue since tests don't compare across. Fine.

Also note: the contended-runner test itself uses `asciiProse` with the shared RNG — fine.

4. **The flat-clock test**: `elapsedUs: (_) => 5000` — constant 5000µs for every measurement. - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1534
- **Title**: gh-1532 FLAKE: wrap_ansi_line_perf_test timing assertion (2x input = 3.2x time) red on loaded runner
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1532` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 1
- **Additions**: +118
- **Deletions**: -21
- **Created**: 2026-10-11T06:31:08Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-11T07:02:35Z

## PR Description

Closes #1532
### Root Cause

- `expectLinearGrowth` in `test/cli/wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart` took a **single** doubling-ratio sample: ~3.8ms baseline (100k ASCII cells) vs ~7.2ms doubled, gated at 3.2x while linear measures ~2.0x. On a runner contended by release windows, one scheduler steal/GC pause of a few ms inside either `Stopwatch` window inflates that lone sample past 3.2x — the gh-1532 live failure (fa run 38113730068).
- Sub-5ms single-shot timing assertions are inherently unstable on shared runners; median-of-5 per size was not enough because a sustained steal contaminates ≥3 of 5 runs.

### Fix

- `test/cli/wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart` — `expectLinearGrowth` now takes **3 independent doubling attempts** and gates the superlinear guard on the **min** ratio: contention can only add wall time, so the min approaches the uncontended ratio. A genuine regression (~4x+ quadratic shape) still fails under min, in every attempt.
- Added a **meaningful-growth lower bound** (max ratio across attempts must exceed 1.5x; linear ≈ 2x) so the retry-min cannot become a rubber stamp — a degenerate flat measurement now fails (AC2).
- Threaded an injectable `ElapsedUs` clock through `medianWrapMs`/`expectLinearGrowth` (default: real `Stopwatch`, unchanged behavior) so contention is reproduced **deterministically** via `contendedClock` instead of by CI luck.
- No production changes (`wrapAnsiLine` untouched) — the flake was in the test harness only.

### Test Coverage

- RED first: both new tests failed pre-fix (the hermetic seam did not exist; the flat-clock scenario passed the old assertion while asserting nothing).
- `growth assertion survives a contended-runner preemption spike (gh-1532)` — 30ms fake preemption across 3 timed runs of one measurement (~9x ratio for that attempt) is discarded; PASSED.
- `growth assertion rejects a degenerate flat measurement (gh-1532)` — constant clock (ratio 1.0) must throw `TestFailure`; PASSED.
- Guard not weakened: spiking the doubled measurement in **all 3 attempts** still fails with a 7.09x min ratio.
- Perf file: 8/8 PASSED. `dart analyze` clean, `dart format` applied.
- Full unit suite (CI invocation `dart test --exclude-tags integration`): 10235 passed / 0 failed / 10 skipped; full-discovery JSON reporter confirms both gh-1532 tests execute and pass in-suite.

### Notes

- The absolute 100ms-budget tests were not flaking (median-of-5 over ~10–20ms workloads tolerates outliers) and are unchanged.
- Test names unchanged — "2x input <= 3.2x time" still describes the gate, now applied to the best-of-3-attempts ratio.
- The lower bound (1.5x) sits well below the measured linear ratio (~1.9–2.0x locally across all three shapes) and uses the max across attempts, so jitter cannot push it under the bound without also being visible as a measurement failure elsewhere.
- An earlier broad `dart test` run (including integration-tagged suites) hit 13 failures + a native `malloc_consolidate` abort on this loaded runner under a non-CI tag selection; the CI-equivalent unit invocation above is fully green, and targeted runs of the affected integration files are unrelated to this test-only change.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),

1. **Does the fix actually solve the flake?** The contention model: contention can only ADD wall time — that's the claim used for gating on min. But wait: is that claim correct? Contention adds wall time to both `small` and `doubled` measurements. If contention inflates both equally (additive), the ratio inflates when the small measurement is inflated. Ratio = doubled/small. If the small measurement gets +X ms spike and doubled gets none, ratio decreases. If doubled gets spike, ratio increases. Gating on min across attempts: for the min ratio to be inflated, the doubled measurement must be spiked in EVERY attempt while the small one is not. Possible but much rarer. OK.

2. **The `minRatio` guard uses `lessThan(maxLinearRatio)`** — strictly less than 3.2. Measured linear ratio ~2.0x. Fine.

3. **The new spiked test**: `contendedClock(spiked: {6, 7, 8})`. Measurement call order: per attempt, 5 timed runs of small then 5 of doubled. Attempt 1: calls 1-5 small, 6-10 doubled. So spikes {6,7,8} are the first three timed runs of the doubled measurement in attempt 1. Median of 5 = 3rd value after sorting. Spiked values: times ~[t+30, t+30, t+30, t, t] sorted → [t, t, t+30, t+30, t+30], median = t+30. Hmm! Median of 5 with 3 spiked = spiked value. So the doubled median in attempt 1 is ~baseline+30ms ≈ 7.2+30 = ~37ms vs small ~3.8ms → ratio ~9x. That's what the comment says (~9x ratio for that attempt). Attempts 2,3 are unspiked → ratio ~2x → min ratio ~2x → passes. OK.

Also note: the contended-runner test itself uses `asciiProse` with the shared RNG — fine.

Actually wait — is "contention can only ADD wall time" fully true? GC pauses, yes they add. Scheduler steals add. Fine.

6. **Performance cost**: 3 attempts × 2 sizes × (1 warmup + 5 runs) = 36 wrap calls per growth test × 3 growth tests = 108 wraps of 100k-200k cells. Pre-existing was 36. Test time roughly triples, maybe ~100ms extra per test. Negligible.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1534
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1534
- **Title**: gh-1532 FLAKE: wrap_ansi_line_perf_test timing assertion (2x input = 3.2x time) red on loaded runner
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1532` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 1
- **Additions**: +118
- **Deletions**: -21
- **Created**: 2026-10-11T06:31:08Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-11T07:02:35Z

## PR Description

Closes #1532
### Root Cause

- `expectLinearGrowth` in `test/cli/wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart` took a **single** doubling-ratio sample: ~3.8ms baseline (100k ASCII cells) vs ~7.2ms doubled, gated at 3.2x while linear measures ~2.0x. On a runner contended by release windows, one scheduler steal/GC pause of a few ms inside either `Stopwatch` window inflates that lone sample past 3.2x — the gh-1532 live failure (fa run 38113730068).
- Sub-5ms single-shot timing assertions are inherently unstable on shared runners; median-of-5 per size was not enough because a sustained steal contaminates ≥3 of 5 runs.

### Fix

- `test/cli/wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart` — `expectLinearGrowth` now takes **3 independent doubling attempts** and gates the superlinear guard on the **min** ratio: contention can only add wall time, so the min approaches the uncontended ratio. A genuine regression (~4x+ quadratic shape) still fails under min, in every attempt.
- Added a **meaningful-growth lower bound** (max ratio across attempts must exceed 1.5x; linear ≈ 2x) so the retry-min cannot become a rubber stamp — a degenerate flat measurement now fails (AC2).
- Threaded an injectable `ElapsedUs` clock through `medianWrapMs`/`expectLinearGrowth` (default: real `Stopwatch`, unchanged behavior) so contention is reproduced **deterministically** via `contendedClock` instead of by CI luck.
- No production changes (`wrapAnsiLine` untouched) — the flake was in the test harness only.

### Test Coverage

- RED first: both new tests failed pre-fix (the hermetic seam did not exist; the flat-clock scenario passed the old assertion while asserting nothing).
- `growth assertion survives a contended-runner preemption spike (gh-1532)` — 30ms fake preemption across 3 timed runs of one measurement (~9x ratio for that attempt) is discarded; PASSED.
- `growth assertion rejects a degenerate flat measurement (gh-1532)` — constant clock (ratio 1.0) must throw `TestFailure`; PASSED.
- Guard not weakened: spiking the doubled measurement in **all 3 attempts** still fails with a 7.09x min ratio.
- Perf file: 8/8 PASSED. `dart analyze` clean, `dart format` applied.
- Full unit suite (CI invocation `dart test --exclude-tags integration`): 10235 passed / 0 failed / 10 skipped; full-discovery JSON reporter confirms both gh-1532 tests execute and pass in-suite.

### Notes

- The absolute 100ms-budget tests were not flaking (median-of-5 over ~10–20ms workloads tolerates outliers) and are unchanged.
- Test names unchanged — "2x input <= 3.2x time" still describes the gate, now applied to the best-of-3-attempts ratio.
- The lower bound (1.5x) sits well below the measured linear ratio (~1.9–2.0x locally across all three shapes) and uses the max across attempts, so jitter cannot push it under the bound without also being visible as a measurement failure elsewhere.
- An earlier broad `dart test` run (including integration-tagged suites) hit 13 failures + a native `malloc_consolidate` abort on this loaded runner under a non-CI tag selection; the CI-equivalent unit invocation above is fully green, and targeted runs of the affected integration files are unrelated to this test-only change.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction evictio…

The AGENTS.md is long; I have the conventions. Now let me read the full changed file, and check for CI failures files (there are none input — no ci_failures.md, no pr_discussions.md). So CI status unknown; PR description claims all green.

Now let me analyze carefully.

Key review questions:

1. **Does the fix actually solve the flake?** The contention model: contention can only ADD wall time — that's the claim used for gating on min. But wait: is that claim correct? Contention adds wall time to both `small` and `doubled` measurements. If contention inflates both equally (additive), the ratio inflates when the small measurement is inflated. Ratio = doubled/small. If the small measurement gets +X ms spike and doubled gets none, ratio decreases. If doubled gets spike, ratio increases. Gating on min across attempts: for the min ratio to be inflated, the doubled measurement must be spiked in EVERY attempt while the small one is not. Possible but much rarer. OK.

2. **The `minRatio` guard uses `lessThan(maxLinearRatio)`** — strictly less than 3.2. Measured linear ratio ~2.0x. Fine.

3. **The new spiked test**: `contendedClock(spiked: {6, 7, 8})`. Measurement call order: per attempt, 5 timed runs of small then 5 of doubled. Attempt 1: calls 1-5 small, 6-10 doubled. So spikes {6,7,8} are the first three timed runs of the doubled measurement in attempt 1. Median of 5 = 3rd value after sorting. Spiked values: times ~[t+30, t+30, t+30, t, t] sorted → [t, t, t+30, t+30, t+30], median = t+30. Hmm! Median of 5 with 3 spiked = spiked value. So the doubled median in attempt 1 is ~baseline+30ms ≈ 7.2+30 = ~37ms vs small ~3.8ms → ratio ~9x. That's what the comment says (~9x ratio for that attempt). Attempts 2,3 are unspiked → ratio ~2x → min ratio ~2x → passes. OK.

Wait — but the call counter: each `medianWrapMs` does 1 warm-up (untimed) + 5 timed. The warm-up doesn't call `measure` — it calls `wrapAnsiLine` directly. Yes: `wrapAnsiLine(line, width); // JIT warm-up, untimed` — not through measure. So timed calls: attempt 1: 1-5 small, 6-10 doubled. Correct.

But wait — `asciiProse` uses the shared `_rng = Random(1496)` — the RNG is a top-level final, shared across calls and tests! `build(baseCells)` is called per attempt: `asciiProse(1000)` three times in the growth test, producing *different strings* per attempt since the RNG continues. That's pre-existing behavior (the old code also called build once per size, so old: 2 calls; new: 6 calls per growth test). Different content per attempt adds variance, but content is similar distribution. Not a new issue but the tripled number of `build` calls consumes the shared RNG stream, which changes what subsequent tests generate — no correctness issue since tests don't compare across. Fine.

Also note: the contended-runner test itself uses `asciiProse` with the shared RNG — fine.

4. **The flat-clock test**: `elapsedUs: (_) => 5000` — constant 5000µs for every measurement. Ratio = 1.0 each attempt. minRatio = 1.0 < 3.2 passes first expect; maxRatio = 1.0, `greaterThan(1.5)` fails → TestFailure. Good. But wait — does it throw TestFailure? `expect(maxRatio, greaterThan(minGrowthRatio), reason: ...)` — yes, throws TestFailure. Test passes.

Hmm, but there's a subtle issue: in the flat-clock test, the first expect passes (minRatio 1.0 < 3.2) and the second fails. If someone reordered or the first also failed, throwsA still catches TestFailure. Fine.

5. **minRatio guard: `lessThan(3.2)`** — with attempts=3 on a genuinely contended runner where every attempt is mildly inflated: e.g., all attempts measure 3.3x because of sustained background load during the whole test — still fails. That's the residual flake risk; the min-of-3 reduces probability. Acceptable design; PR acknowledges contention can only add time.

Actually wait — is "contention can only ADD wall time" fully true? GC pauses, yes they add. Scheduler steals add. Fine.

6. **Performance cost**: 3 attempts × 2 sizes × (1 warmup + 5 runs) = 36 wrap calls per growth test × 3 growth tests = 108 wraps of 100k-200k cells. Pre-existing was 36. Test time roughly triples, maybe ~100ms extra per test. Negligible.

7. **`contendedClock` spike applied based on global call counter across both small and doubled** — the doc comment says "adds spike to the timed measurements whose 1-based index is in spiked". The test relies on exact call ordering, documented in the comment. OK but brittle: if `medianWrapMs` is changed to add more timed runs, indices shift silently and the test would spike the wrong calls — possibly still passing while asserting nothing about the intended scenario? Let's check: if `runs` changed to 7, calls 6,7,8 would be small's runs 6,7 — then small median gets spiked → ratio decreased → test trivially passes but no longer tests the intended scenario. It's a suggestion-level robustness note.

8. **The `spiked` set-based index addressing**: similar brittleness. SUGGESTION.

9. **`double spikeMs = 30` default param unused flexibility** — fine.

10. **Doc mismatch in test names**: "2x input <= 3.2x time" still describes... fine per PR.

11. **Does the min-ratio approach weaken the guard against genuine superlinear regression?** A regression at ratio 3.3x in all 3 attempts still fails. A regression at ratio 3.1x (just below gate) passes — same as before. Fine.

12. **Real subtle concern**: the lower-bound guard `maxRatio > 1.5`. On a heavily contended runner where the SMALL measurement always gets the big GC pause and doubled doesn't... ratios drop below 1.5? Ratio = doubled/small. If small is inflated consistently while doubled isn't — improbable since doubled runs longer. Max across 3 attempts of a linear measurement ≈ 2.0 with jitter; jitter would have to push all 3 attempts' ratios below 1.5 — meaning the small measurement consistently took >33% longer than doubled, implausible. Fine.

13. **Warm-up not timed but the fake clock counts only timed calls** — good, the warm-up is genuinely untimed via direct call.

14. **`_stopwatchUs` as top-level private function; `ElapsedUs` typedef public within test file** — test-only file, fine.

15. **`medianWrapMs` signature change**: added optional named param `elapsedUs` — backward compatible within the file. Any other callers of `medianWrapMs`/`expectLinearGrowth` elsewhere? Let me grep.

16. Line 95-ish: `contendedClock` — `calls++` after `sw.stop()`. If body throws, calls not incremented — wrapAnsiLine doesn't throw. Fine.

17. **AGENTS.md conventions**: god-file ceiling 2800 lines — file is ~250 lines, fine. Dart format applied.

18. Check whether `dart analyze` would flag anything: `ElapsedUs? elapsedUs` unused default fine. `contendedClock` returns closure capturing `calls` — fine.

19. One more: the doc comment in the file header says "The growth asserts take several independent attempts and gate on the min ratio" — accurate.

20. **Attempts share JIT warm-up?** Each `medianWrapMs` call does its own warm-up, good.

21. Potential issue: in the contended test, attempt 1's doubled measurement median is inflated to ~37ms; min ratio comes from attempts 2/3 ≈ 2.0 < 3.2 pass. Max ratio ~9 > 1.5 pass. Test passes deterministically regardless of real Stopwatch jitter? The real elapsed times factor in too: ratio for attempts 2,3 ≈ real ratio ~2. Could real jitter push min ratio ≥ 3.2 in this *hermetic* test? Attempts 2 and 3 have no spikes, so min ratio = the smaller of two unspiked ratios ≈ 2.0 ± jitter. On a heavily loaded CI runner could a single unspiked doubling sample hit 3.2x? That's exactly what the fix claims is rare — min of 3 attempts. But in this test only 2 of 3 attempts are informative. Fine.

But wait — the spiked attempt's ratio: doubled median ≈ 37ms, small median ≈ 3.8ms → ~9.7x. maxRatio ≈ 9.7 > 1.5. Passes.

Hmm, but one edge: what if the spike set {6,7,8} with 5-run median: sorted [t,t+30,t+30,t+30] → median = t+30. Yes.

22. Check the PR claim "spiking the doubled measurement in all 3 attempts still fails with a 7.09x min ratio": spiked calls would be {6,7,8,16,17,18,26,27,28}. Each attempt's doubled median +30ms → ratio ~9.7x each → min ~9.7? They say 7.09x. Whatever, it fails. Not something I need to verify exactly.

Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. # AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction evictio…

If the small measurement gets +X ms spike and doubled gets none, ratio decreases. If doubled gets spike, ratio increases. Gating on min across attempts: for the min ratio to be inflated, the doubled measurement must be spiked in EVERY attempt while the small one is not. Possible but much rarer. OK.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1534
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1534
- **Title**: gh-1532 FLAKE: wrap_ansi_line_perf_test timing assertion (2x input = 3.2x time) red on loaded runner
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1532` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 1
- **Additions**: +118
- **Deletions**: -21
- **Created**: 2026-10-11T06:31:08Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-11T07:02:35Z

## PR Description

Closes #1532
### Root Cause

- `expectLinearGrowth` in `test/cli/wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart` took a **single** doubling-ratio sample: ~3.8ms baseline (100k ASCII cells) vs ~7.2ms doubled, gated at 3.2x while linear measures ~2.0x. On a runner contended by release windows, one scheduler steal/GC pause of a few ms inside either `Stopwatch` window inflates that lone sample past 3.2x — the gh-1532 live failure (fa run 38113730068).
- Sub-5ms single-shot timing assertions are inherently unstable on shared runners; median-of-5 per size was not enough because a sustained steal contaminates ≥3 of 5 runs.

### Fix

- `test/cli/wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart` — `expectLinearGrowth` now takes **3 independent doubling attempts** and gates the superlinear guard on the **min** ratio: contention can only add wall time, so the min approaches the uncontended ratio. A genuine regression (~4x+ quadratic shape) still fails under min, in every attempt.
- Added a **meaningful-growth lower bound** (max ratio across attempts must exceed 1.5x; linear ≈ 2x) so the retry-min cannot become a rubber stamp — a degenerate flat measurement now fails (AC2).
- Threaded an injectable `ElapsedUs` clock through `medianWrapMs`/`expectLinearGrowth` (default: real `Stopwatch`, unchanged behavior) so contention is reproduced **deterministically** via `contendedClock` instead of by CI luck.
- No production changes (`wrapAnsiLine` untouched) — the flake was in the test harness only.

### Test Coverage

- RED first: both new tests failed pre-fix (the hermetic seam did not exist; the flat-clock scenario passed the old assertion while asserting nothing).
- `growth assertion survives a contended-runner preemption spike (gh-1532)` — 30ms fake preemption across 3 timed runs of one measurement (~9x ratio for that attempt) is discarded; PASSED.
- `growth assertion rejects a degenerate flat measurement (gh-1532)` — constant clock (ratio 1.0) must throw `TestFailure`; PASSED.
- Guard not weakened: spiking the doubled measurement in **all 3 attempts** still fails with a 7.09x min ratio.
- Perf file: 8/8 PASSED. `dart analyze` clean, `dart format` applied.
- Full unit suite (CI invocation `dart test --exclude-tags integration`): 10235 passed / 0 failed / 10 skipped; full-discovery JSON reporter confirms both gh-1532 tests execute and pass in-suite.

### Notes

- The absolute 100ms-budget tests were not flaking (median-of-5 over ~10–20ms workloads tolerates outliers) and are unchanged.
- Test names unchanged — "2x input <= 3.2x time" still describes the gate, now applied to the best-of-3-attempts ratio.
- The lower bound (1.5x) sits well below the measured linear ratio (~1.9–2.0x locally across all three shapes) and uses the max across attempts, so jitter cannot push it under the bound without also being visible as a measurement failure elsewhere.
- An earlier broad `dart test` run (including integration-tagged suites) hit 13 failures + a native `malloc_consolidate` abort on this loaded runner under a non-CI tag selection; the CI-equivalent unit invocation above is fully green, and targeted runs of the affected integration files are unrelated to this test-only change.
